subject: Routing boundaries & streaming SLA playbook for HealthGrid pilot
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam@healthgrid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Routing boundaries & streaming SLA playbook for HealthGrid pilot

Hi Liam — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so everything is captured in one place.

Summary of requirements you confirmed on the call:
- Target p95 token-generation latency: 120ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens); p95 <= 250ms for mid requests (129-1024 tokens).
- Sustained throughput goal: ~1.2M tokens/hour during peak; concurrency target: 250 concurrent sessions (typical session = streaming chat connection).
- Streaming expectation: server-sent-events / chunked responses with <50ms inter-chunk lag (p95) for active sessions.
- Geo routing & residency: primary US region for US customers; EU traffic must terminate in eu-west-1 and remain in EU boundary (no LLMS routing outside EU). APAC traffic prefers ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) where available.
- Fallbacks: accept automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant (gptx-q4_8k) on capacity alerts, with a configurable quality threshold.

Questions we still need from you to finalize the pilot scope:
1) Can you share a representative sample of request size distribution (attached CSV sample helps) — particularly token length percentiles and average streaming chunk sizes?
2) Confirm whether sessions are sticky at client-level (session affinity) or can be redistributed across instances mid-session.
3) Any contractual constraints on percent of requests that may be served outside primary region during emergency failover?

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Diego: prepare pilot perf-run plan (load profile, region split, test checkpoints) — by Thu 2026-09-16 EOD.
- Marissa: produce SLA playbook draft (fallback thresholds, alerting, escalations) — by Mon 2026-09-20.
- HealthGrid (Liam): return sample telemetry and confirm session affinity model — by Fri 2026-09-17.

Attached: healthgrid-pilot-spec.pdf (pilot timeline & perf test plan), healthgrid-sample-load.csv (sample payload distribution).

If that matches your notes, we can kick off a 2-week pilot next week and run a cross-region soak to validate routing and streaming SLOs.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Attachments: healthgrid-pilot-spec.pdf (21 KB), healthgrid-sample-load.csv (12 KB)
From: Liam Chen <liam@healthgrid.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthGrid engineering team <eng@healthgrid.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 17:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Routing boundaries & streaming SLA playbook for HealthGrid pilot

Diego — this is great, thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- We'll attach a CSV with token percentiles and a short description of session stickiness. We do prefer session affinity (authentication token tied to session) but we can accept mid-session handover for read-only interactions; live editing sessions must remain sticky.
- For EU residency: legal requires primary processing in EU and backups within EU as well. Failover to US is allowed only after a documented incident and with explicit notification to our security team (we cannot accept uncontrolled cross-border routing).
- For APAC, latency from Singapore to our customers in APAC is adequate; we can also accept routing to Tokyo if Singapore is saturated.

Can you confirm what monitoring hooks you'll expose during the pilot (we need per-region p95 and per-model variant counts)? Also send the HubSpot or doc link you referenced for the pilot resources.

We are OK to start the two-week pilot on Monday 2026-09-20 pending acceptance of the DPA and the pilot SOW.

—Liam
Liam Chen
Head of Platform Engineering | HealthGrid
liam@healthgrid.ai
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam@healthgrid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:13:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Routing boundaries & streaming SLA playbook for HealthGrid pilot

Thanks Liam — understood on the EU backup constraint and session stickiness nuance. A couple quick confirmations: 

- Monitoring hooks: we will provide a temporary read-only dashboard per-region (US/EU/APAC) with p50/p95/p99 latency, streaming inter-chunk latency distribution, tokens/sec, and active concurrency. We will also emit per-request model-variant tag (e.g., gptx-1 / gptx-q4_8k) so you can see fallback ratios.
- Access & links: HubSpot timeline is HS-987654; drive folder (pilot artifacts) is shared to your liam@healthgrid.ai address — link included below.
- DPA: our legal team will share a DPA template today; please flag any required edits.

Internal note for Marissa/Rishi: HealthGrid insists on EU-only backups unless incident-triggered notification and approval. They want per-region dashboards and model-variant telemetry. Please add a runbook section for explicit cross-border failover approvals and an API key tagging strategy for session affinity.

I'll start the perf-run plan today and kick off a small cross-region soak during the pilot — scope attached in the pilot-spec.

Diego
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 15:41:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Routing boundaries & streaming SLA playbook for HealthGrid pilot

Diego / Rishi — drafting the SLA playbook now. Notes I'm adding so we can be prescriptive in the document: 

- Definitions: short = <=128 tokens, mid = 129-1024, long = >1024 (affects batch sizing & kernel selection).
- SLOs we will propose in the playbook: regional p95 latency targets (short: <=120ms | mid: <=250ms | long: best-effort), streaming inter-chunk p95 <=50ms, availability target = 99.9% during pilot window.
- Pilot validation steps: 24h baseline (no failover), 72h cross-region soak with 20% traffic diverted to EU/APAC to validate routing + cache warmups, 2 controlled failover drills (EU->EU backup and EU->US emergency) — but per HealthGrid request, EU->US emergency requires documented approval flow.
- Observability: include webhook for HealthGrid's PagerDuty and read-only access to per-region dashboard. Add log retention options (30/90/365 days) as configurable add-on.

Action: I'll circulate a one-page SLO summary and a short runbook by EOD Monday (2026-09-20) so legal & engineering can sign off. Rishi — can you validate expected token/sec for the quantized fallback variant and note any expected quality delta to include in the playbook?

Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
